config.title: Test User Interactions

intro.title: Test User Interactions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive button component and write tests to verify that it responds correctly to user clicks. You'll learn how to simulate user interactions in a React testing environment using React Testing Library. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and Jest with the user-event library. By the end, you'll understand how to ensure your components behave as expected when users interact with them.
intro.usecase: Testing user interactions is essential for ensuring that interactive UI components work correctly in real applications. For example, form validation in sign-up flows, button clicks in e-commerce checkout processes, and filter selections in data dashboards all require reliable interaction testing. Developers use these tests to catch regressions when adding new features or refactoring code, preventing bugs that could frustrate users. In products like admin panels, modal dialogs, and navigation menus, thorough interaction testing helps maintain a smooth, predictable user experience across updates.

objectives: Implement a React component with TypeScript that includes interactive elements for user testing.
Initialize and manage component state to track user interactions within a test scenario.
Construct event handlers to respond to user inputs like clicks and form submissions.
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the shape of props and state for type-safe interaction testing.
Render conditional UI feedback based on the state changes triggered by user actions.
Integrate user interaction tests by simulating events and verifying the resulting component behavior.
Configure a testing environment to run and evaluate user interaction tests effectively.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing modules for a project
import { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to build a React component with state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported React and useState correctly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named InteractionTest with proper TypeScript typing. The component should return null for now.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax with TypeScript. Make sure to specify the return type.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the InteractionTest component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named InteractionTest is defined with TypeScript typing and returns null.
successCriteria: The InteractionTest component is defined with proper TypeScript typing and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'InteractionTest' and has proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you used the exact name 'InteractionTest' and included TypeScript typing.

steps.title: Initialize state for click count
steps.instruction: Inside the InteractionTest component, initialize a state variable named clickCount using useState, starting with a value of 0.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the initial value (0) and destructure the returned array.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a clickCount state variable initialized to 0, ready to track button clicks.
successCriteria: The clickCount state variable is declared using useState with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with the correct initial value (0) and naming the variable clickCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clickCount state variable isn't properly initialized. Remember to use useState(0) and name the variable clickCount.

steps.title: Initialize state for input text
steps.instruction: Inside the InteractionTest component, add a second useState hook to create a state variable named inputText, initialized as an empty string.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useState again with an initial value of '' and destructure the returned array into inputText and setInputText.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: another useState for text
const [text, setText] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two state variables: clickCount and inputText, both managed with useState.
successCriteria: A state variable named inputText is declared with useState, initialized as an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're declaring inputText with useState and initializing it as ''.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match. You need to add a second useState call for inputText inside the component.

steps.title: Define click handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the InteractionTest component, define a function named handleClick that increments the clickCount state by 1.
steps.hint: You can create a function that calls setClickCount with the current count plus one. Use the state setter function to update the state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleClick function is defined inside the component that increments clickCount when called.
successCriteria: The handleClick function is defined, uses setClickCount, and increments the clickCount state by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it increments clickCount by 1 using setClickCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleClick function is not defined correctly. It should increment clickCount by 1 using setClickCount.

steps.title: Add container structure
steps.instruction: In your InteractionTest component, return a div container with the className 'interaction-container'.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a JSX div element that has the specified className.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div container with the className 'interaction-container'.
successCriteria: The component returns a JSX div element with className='interaction-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div element with the exact className 'interaction-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div container with className='interaction-container'. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Add click counter display
steps.instruction: Inside the InteractionTest component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current clickCount value.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to create a

tag and insert the clickCount state variable inside curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in a paragraph

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the click count value inside a paragraph element.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the return statement that displays the clickCount value using curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the clickCount value using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element displaying clickCount is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add click button with event handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the container div with an onClick event handler wired to the handleClick function and the text 'Click me'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with the onClick prop set to the handleClick function. Remember to include the button text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element appears in the container div with the text 'Click me' and an onClick handler that will call the handleClick function when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element is added with onClick={handleClick} and displays the text 'Click me'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing either the onClick handler or the correct text. Make sure to include onClick={handleClick} and the text 'Click me'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is not present or doesn't match the requirements. Add a <button> element with onClick={handleClick} and the text 'Click me'.

steps.title: Add text input with change handler
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add an input element with its value bound to inputText state and its onChange event wired to handleInputChange.
steps.hint: Use the input element with type='text', value={inputText}, and onChange={handleInputChange}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: controlled input element
<input type="text" value={someState} onChange={handleChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will be added to the UI, allowing text input that updates the inputText state through the change handler.
successCriteria: An input element with type='text', value={inputText}, and onChange={handleInputChange} is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure it has both value={inputText} and onChange={handleInputChange} attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or doesn't have the correct attributes. Add an input with type='text', value={inputText}, and onChange={handleInputChange}.
